title: Grateful Dead Live at Sacramento Memorial Auditorium on 1972-08-12
source: Source Info: 7" Master Soundboard Reels @7.5ips 1/2trk > Garcia's reel @ 3.75 ips > Will Boswell's reel @ 3.75 ips (Maxell UDXL); Transfer Info: Technics RS1506 > Tascam DA-3000 > Adobe Audition > TLH flac2496

ai_review.summary: An exceptional August 12‑1972 Sacramento performance captured on an excellent soundboard, with only a handful of splice cuts.
ai_review.review: The show is hailed as one of the quintessential post‑Europe ’72 concerts – tight, high‑energy playing with standout moments like “Black Throated Wind,” “Playing In The Band,” and a ferocious “One More Saturday Night.”  The soundboard source is praised for its clarity and overall quality, though several songs contain noticeable cuts that slightly detract from the listening experience.

ai_rating.rationale: Review rates the show 5 stars and describes it as a near‑perfect performance; recording is rated excellent despite minor splice issues, yielding an overall rating in the high‑range.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear and balanced soundboard, but several splices cut portions of El Paso, Tennessee Jed, Jack Straw, Greatest Story intro, The Other One, and Sugar Magnolia.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Tight, well‑sequenced set with seamless transitions; early songs build momentum leading to extended jams and a high‑octane second set.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Multiple mentions of his massive solo work, wah‑pedal tone in Playing In The Band, ferocious solos on many tunes, and emotive vocals on Black Peter.
band_member_comments.Phil: Highlighted for explosive bass runs (especially the iconic intro to The Other One) and wild playing throughout the jams.
band_member_comments.Bob: Praised for powerful vocal performances on songs like Beat It On Down The Line and One More Saturday Night.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith Godchaux lauded for “killer jazzy piano leads,” perfect piano licks on Black Throated Wind, Stella Blue, and other moments; described as playing his balls off.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann’s drumming called aggressive, technical, kick‑ass, and driving the band hard through jams.
